title: Loam and the Fracture
loopLine: Farm / hunt / defend · World map adventure
hook: **Loam** is the pressure of ground you hold on the rift map — neglect it and the **Fracture** fades that holding away. It never banks and never crosses to another world.

blindSpots.meaning: A **world stock** tied to sectors you hold. It is position and upkeep, not a wallet you carry forever.
The force that unmakes ground you do not keep real. Neglect → fade → loss. Not a combat status.
What souls and essence do across worlds. Loam does **not** bank — when you advance, loam and that world’s holdings stay with the world you left.
A place on the rift map you can claim, march through, or lose. Loam stories live on sectors.

alsoTrue: Loam belongs to this world only, like rubble, ironwork, and recruits. [Souls](souls) and [essence](essence) bank across worlds. Nothing converts into loam.
The surface is playable but thin in this build — deeper empire verbs and buildings are still catching up.

sections.title: What it is
paras: Every sector carries a loam story: fertile ground supports an expanding empire; barren ground drains one.
Territory you neglect fades, then is lost to the Fracture. Structures die with the fade; some natural rootbeds remain as places you can found on again.
sections.note: Advancing keeps your roster, souls, and essence — not loam. See [Advancing to a new world](new-world-prestige).

sections.title: Why it exists
paras: Without a stock that stays with its world, empire play collapses into “farm forever, then leave.”
Loam makes holding ground a real choice: expand, maintain, or lose what you claimed.

sections.title: How it works
sections.intro: Think in map verbs, not shop tabs:

cards.name: Hold
cards.body: Claimed sectors stay real while their loam story supports them.

cards.name: Neglect
cards.body: Fade is gradual and visible — you get a chance to notice before the Fracture takes the holding.

cards.name: Spend
cards.body: Buildings and position cost loam (sometimes with essence). That is the farm beat of empire.

diagram: claim sector  ->  loam pressure on that ground

groups.title: On the rift map
groups.intro: Open World travel when you are ready to march.
steps: Travel to the world map from Sanctum.
Read loam on sectors you hold or want.
Watch for fade on neglected ground before it is gone.
groups.note: Sector buildings that spend loam are still WIP as a full farm loop — see [sector buildings](sector-buildings).

doSteps: Open the world map when travel is available.
Claim or inspect a sector and notice its loam story.
Decide once: hold it (come back) or leave it — neglect is a choice with a cost.
doNote: Stop when you can say why loam is not a second soul bank. Next: [farm / hunt / defend](farm-hunt-defend) and the [world map](world-map).

mixUps.q: Can I save loam for the next world?
mixUps.a: No. Loam never crosses worlds; it stays with the world you left. Roster, souls, and essence bank.

mixUps.q: Is loam the same as souls?
mixUps.a: No. Souls buy roster power. Loam buys and keeps ground. See [souls](souls).

mixUps.q: Does essence fade with the Fracture?
mixUps.a: No. Only loam and neglected holdings. Essence banks — see [essence](essence).

mixUps.q: If ground fades, is my whole save wiped?
mixUps.a: No. You lose that holding’s position on the map. Your summoner bank (roster, souls, essence) remains.

mixUps.q: Is the Fracture a boss I fight?
mixUps.a: Not as a single boss fight. It is the rule that unanchored ground stops being real.
